stories.headline: Update: Nepal-China Flood Death Toll Reaches 1,375 as Rescuers Pull Survivors from Tunnels Ten Days On
stories.summary:
Rescuers in Nepal pulled a Chinese national alive from a hydropower tunnel and a 60-year-old woman from the upper floor of a flooded building on Saturday, ten days after catastrophic flash floods struck the Nepal-China border region. The dramatic rescues follow a similar operation the day prior, when two men were extracted from another hydropower tunnel using satellite imagery to locate it beneath layers of mud. Hundreds of tunnel workers remain missing.

The confirmed death toll has climbed to 1,375, according to a CNN tally of figures from Nepali and Chinese authorities, with more than 5,000 people still unaccounted for. Over 7,500 homes have been damaged, affecting nearly 33,000 people directly, while approximately 84,000 are estimated to require urgent humanitarian assistance. Thirteen hydropower projects, 37 vehicle bridges, and nearly 4,500 acres of agricultural land have been damaged.

The United Nations and its humanitarian partners launched an appeal Friday for $49.6 million to provide emergency shelter, food, and healthcare to affected communities. 'Families have lost everything: their loved ones, their homes, their livelihoods, swept away in minutes,' said UN resident coordinator Lila Pieters Yahia. The scale of infrastructure destruction has complicated both rescue operations and the broader relief response.

stories.headline: Explosion at Bolivia Military Barracks Kills at Least Two, Injures 81 Near La Paz
stories.summary:
An explosion ripped through a military barracks in Viacha, Bolivia, approximately 30 kilometers from the capital La Paz, on Friday afternoon local time, killing at least two people and injuring 81 others. Bolivian Defense Minister Ernesto Justiniano said 'pyrotechnic material' detonated at the site, where an artillery regiment was stationed. Seven people remain missing, and a local health official told television reporters that between 10 and 15 people were believed to have died.

The blast caused significant collateral damage, destroying dozens of nearby homes. Authorities warned residents to remain at least 150 meters from the military base due to the risk of a secondary explosion. Emergency workers continued to search rubble for survivors and victims into Friday evening.

Bolivian President Rodrigo Paz expressed solidarity with affected families and pledged a 'thorough, technical and transparent investigation' into the cause of the blast. The city of Viacha declared three days of official mourning. The cause remains under investigation, though police confirmed that fireworks had been stored at the barracks.

stories.headline: Russia's Africa Corps Credited with Suppressing Niger Military Mutiny, Deepening Sahel Dependency on Moscow
stories.summary:
Russia's Africa Corps helped Nigerien loyalist forces retake a strategic military base at Diori Hamani International Airport in Niamey last Saturday after mutinous soldiers seized it, with Russia's ambassador to Niger publicly acknowledging the intervention. The episode marks the second time this year Africa Corps has played a decisive role at the same airport, having helped repel a jihadist attack in January. Unlike its predecessor the Wagner Group, Africa Corps operates directly under the Russian Defense Ministry and maintains an estimated 200 to 300 personnel in Niger.

Analysts say the incident illustrates that Russia is providing something increasingly valued by Sahel military governments beyond counterinsurgency support: protection of the regimes themselves. 'This is seen as a symbolic victory that will continue to put them at the centre of not just the counter-insurgency campaign, but even in the protection and prolongation of military rule,' said Beverly Ochieng of Control Risks. The junta that seized power in Niger in July 2023 had justified the coup partly by citing the failure of Western partners to contain jihadist violence.

Three years on, that insurgency remains unresolved. Militants linked to al-Qaeda and Islamic State continue to launch attacks across the Tillabéri and Dosso regions, inflicting heavy casualties. The latest mutiny is attributed to longstanding grievances within Niger's own military compounded by the pressures of sustained counterinsurgency operations, underscoring the fragility of the junta's hold on power even as Moscow consolidates its influence across Niger, Mali, and Burkina Faso.

stories.headline: Update: U.S.-Iran Conflict Enters New Phase as Strikes Continue, Ceasefire Deal Expires
stories.summary:
The U.S.-Iran conflict has entered a more uncertain phase as a Memorandum of Understanding signed in June — intended to produce a permanent ceasefire within 60 days — has expired without resolution. Both sides have exchanged strikes this week, including a U.S. strike on rocket launchers on Larak Island in the Strait of Hormuz that killed two people, followed by Iranian missile and drone retaliatory attacks on U.S. targets in the region. Washington simultaneously announced sweeping new sanctions it described as an 'economic D-Day,' targeting Iran and countries that trade with the regime.

Experts consulted by the BBC offer a divided prognosis. Washington-based analysts suggest the Trump administration is currently satisfied with a form of stasis — maintaining the blockade and conducting periodic strikes on Iranian capabilities — while hoping new economic pressure will bring Tehran to the table in a weakened position. Chatham House analysts, however, argue that Iran is preparing to absorb economic pain and will respond to strikes proportionately to avoid broader escalation, with little indication the squeeze will alter Iranian calculations in the near term.

The Strait of Hormuz, a critical global shipping chokepoint, has been effectively closed since the conflict began in February, though U.S. military escorts have allowed a trickle of oil traffic. Diesel prices in the U.S. have hit record highs as a result. Neither side has articulated a clear off-ramp, and the collapse of the June agreement leaves the path to a negotiated settlement deeply uncertain.

The conflict has now stretched into its seventh month, with the Gaza situation, Houthi activity in Yemen, and tensions in Lebanon adding to regional instability. The Trump administration has said it views Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu's rejection of a related deal as campaign rhetoric, and envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner have been dispatched to Moscow and Kyiv separately for parallel peace diplomacy efforts.

stories.headline: Mistrial Declared in Lindsay Clancy Child Murder Case After Jury Deadlocks
stories.summary:
A Massachusetts judge declared a mistrial Friday in the murder case against Lindsay Clancy, a former nurse charged with strangling her three young children — ages five, three, and eight months — in their Duxbury home in January 2023. The jury deadlocked after seven days of deliberations, signaling three times it could not reach a unanimous verdict. Judge William Sullivan dismissed the panel, telling them, 'At this point, I'm going to declare that the jury is deadlocked and I'm going to declare a mistrial.'

Clancy does not deny killing the children but pleaded not guilty, with her defense arguing she was suffering from severe postpartum psychosis at the time and should not be held criminally responsible. Prosecutors argued she should be held accountable for the killings regardless of her mental state. After the deaths, Clancy cut herself and jumped from a second-story window in a suicide attempt, leaving her paralyzed.

A last-ditch effort by Clancy's attorney Kevin Reddington to have a juror removed — after a note indicated one juror was not following instructions on reasonable doubt — was denied by the judge. The mistrial does not constitute an acquittal; prosecutors retain the option to retry the case or negotiate a plea agreement. A hearing is scheduled for September 29 to determine next steps.

The case drew intense national attention and divided public opinion sharply over questions of mental illness, criminal responsibility, and the adequacy of postpartum psychiatric care. Clancy will remain held on the same murder charges and continue to be housed in a mental health facility pending further proceedings.

stories.headline: Trump Signs Executive Order to Strip Endangered Species Protections from Grey and Mexican Wolves
stories.summary:
President Trump signed an executive order Friday directing Interior Secretary Doug Burgum to determine within 90 days whether grey wolf and Mexican wolf populations have recovered sufficiently to be removed from the federal endangered species list. The order cited ranchers' 'vital role' in the food supply chain and American cultural heritage, and noted that U.S. livestock herds are at a 75-year low while beef demand has risen 10% over the past decade. The move does not immediately authorize ranchers to shoot wolves but opens the pathway for delisting that could remove federal protections.

The Mexican wolf population stands at approximately 319 animals in the wild in the U.S., up from just four when reintroduced in 1998. Grey wolves number roughly 18,000 nationally but remain classified as endangered due to widespread habitat loss. A prior federal effort to delist grey wolves in 2022 was blocked by litigation, and conservation groups signaled they intend to pursue the same legal strategy if the Interior Department acts on this order.

Conservation organizations sharply criticized the move. Greta Anderson of the Western Watersheds Project called it 'a huge distraction to placate a handful of ranchers,' noting that wolf attacks on livestock are statistically rare and that ranchers are already eligible for up to 100% compensation for wolf-caused livestock losses under existing programs. The Wolf Conservation Center warned that weakening protections now would jeopardize decades of recovery work.

The order comes amid broader Trump administration efforts to reduce beef prices for consumers following record highs driven by drought and a livestock parasite outbreak. Ranchers have also expressed frustration with the administration's loosening of beef import restrictions, putting pressure on their margins — making the wolf order partly a political gesture toward agricultural constituencies.

stories.headline: Republican Senate Nominee Ken Paxton Faces Mounting GOP Doubts Ahead of Texas General Election
stories.summary:
Republican Senate nominee Ken Paxton is facing growing concern within his own party as he trails Democratic challenger James Talarico by 2.4 points in the RealClearPolitics polling average, leaving GOP strategists questioning whether national resources should be committed to defending the scandal-tainted, once-impeached Texas attorney general. Veteran Republican strategist Karl Rove warned on Fox News Radio that 'time is running out,' urging President Trump — who endorsed Paxton in the primary runoff over incumbent Sen. John Cornyn — to direct significant financial support toward the race immediately.

Establishment Republicans in Texas and Washington had preferred Cornyn, who lost the runoff by 27.6 points, and are described as having 'mixed emotions' about committing resources to Paxton. Talarico, his Democratic opponent, has out-fundraised Paxton and is running a message centered on Paxton's corruption record. National party officials are simultaneously weighing spending priorities in competitive races in Alaska, Iowa, Ohio, Georgia, North Carolina, Maine, Michigan, New Hampshire, and Minnesota.

The broader Texas Republican ticket is underperforming this cycle, though analysts note a competitive Senate race was likely regardless of the nominee given current political headwinds. The question for national Republicans is whether the Texas media market — among the most expensive in the country — justifies investment when other battlegrounds offer cheaper paths to protecting the Senate majority.

The Texas race illustrates a wider GOP vulnerability heading into the 2026 midterms. Democrats have a generic congressional ballot lead of approximately D+6.6, and Republicans face a historically difficult structural environment for the president's party in midterm cycles. Whether Trump personally intervenes financially on Paxton's behalf is expected to be a decisive factor in the race's outcome.
